executiveChairman.name: Jean Bilong
authority: paid promotion and token grant approval

agentCannot: hold private keys or seed phrases
move BTC, SOL, SATA, or LP tokens
make legal, tax, or investment commitments
promise price, redemption, or market support

items.title: Enable approved-only X social agent posting
items.summary: Allow the X social agent to publish only queue items that the Executive Chairman has already approved.
items.rationale: This gives SATA an operating-company social cadence without allowing agents to invent market claims or approve posts themselves.
items.proposedAction: Set GitHub repo variable SATA_X_AGENT_ENABLE_POSTING=true, add X_ACCESS_TOKEN as a GitHub Actions secret, change social queue mode to approved-only-automation, and approve individual posts before publication.
riskReview: Agent cannot publish unless the specific queue item is marked approved.
No wallet credentials are required.
Posts still pass social policy validation before publishing.
Paid or token-compensated posts remain separate approval items.
items.publicDisclosure: Automated posts must remain factual and source-linked. Paid or token-compensated content requires explicit Sponsored/Paid Partnership disclosure.

items.title: Adopt standard promoter intake policy
items.summary: Require promoter proposals to include deliverables, compensation, draft copy, disclosure policy, and anti-bot confirmation before any payment or token grant.
items.rationale: SATA can work with legitimate promoters only if compensation is disclosed and claims stay factual.
items.proposedAction: Use the promoter intake checklist for every promoter and pay only after the approved deliverable is live and unchanged.
riskReview: Reject fake engagement, pump language, investor targeting, guaranteed results, and undisclosed paid promotion.
Require Sponsored/Paid Partnership disclosure for cash or token compensation.
Keep payment records and public post URLs.
Do not give promoters discretionary posting authority over SATA-owned accounts.
items.publicDisclosure: Sponsored/Paid Partnership. Crypto assets involve risk. No price guarantee, no redemption promise, and liquidity can be thin and volatile.

items.title: Move BTC reserve custody toward multisig as the reserve grows
items.summary: Prepare a staged custody roadmap before the reserve grows materially toward the 1,000,000,000 sats target.
items.rationale: Single-signer custody is acceptable for early speed, but the project needs stronger controls as the reserve becomes material.
items.proposedAction: Draft a public multisig migration plan with signer roles, movement disclosure, verification steps, and fallback procedure.
riskReview: No agent may hold reserve signing keys.
No reserve movement should occur without a public note and chairman approval.
Reserve language must remain transparency-only, not a redemption promise or price floor.
items.publicDisclosure: The BTC reserve is a transparency metric only. It is not a redemption promise, guaranteed price floor, yield product, or market-support commitment.

items.title: Adopt 1,000,000,000 sats reserve growth operating policy
items.summary: Set the operating target at 1,000,000,000 sats while keeping reserve language factual and non-promissory.
items.rationale: The project needs a concrete treasury target, milestones, and funding rules so agents can prepare work without improvising financial commitments.
items.proposedAction: Adopt public reserve-growth-plan.json as the operating reference for reserve milestones, allowed routes, prohibited routes, and chairman approval gates.
riskReview: Reserve growth remains a treasury milestone, not a price guarantee.
Every treasury movement requires chairman approval and public evidence.
Agents may prepare proposals but may not sign transactions.
Any conversion of project assets must be pre-approved, capped, disclosed, and recorded.
items.publicDisclosure: SATA has a long-term treasury milestone of 1,000,000,000 sats. The BTC reserve is a transparency metric only, not a redemption promise, guaranteed price floor, yield product, or market-support commitment.

items.title: Create chairman-approved recurring BTC reserve tranche program
items.summary: Prepare a repeatable process for adding sats to the reserve in disclosed tranches.
items.rationale: Small, recurring, disclosed reserve additions can move SATA toward 1,000,000,000 sats without relying on hype or hidden market activity.
items.proposedAction: Chairman selects tranche size, cadence, source of funds, custody path, and disclosure note before any BTC movement.
riskReview: No tranche may be described as a price-support action.
No tranche may be funded by undisclosed promotion or wash trading.
Each tranche requires transaction evidence and transparency report update.
Cadence should be suspended if operating cash is needed for security, infrastructure, or legal review.
items.publicDisclosure: Reserve additions are treasury transparency events only. No price guarantee, no redemption promise, and no market-support commitment.

items.title: Require public approval before converting dev-held SATA for reserve growth
items.summary: Define strict controls before any dev-held SATA is converted into SOL, BTC, liquidity, operating budget, or reserve assets.
items.rationale: Founder-held SATA is a material concentration risk. Any conversion should be transparent, capped, and approved before execution.
items.proposedAction: Require a chairman-approved proposal with max SATA amount, route, slippage limit, destination, public disclosure text, and post-execution evidence before any conversion.
riskReview: No hidden selling into buyers.
No trading plan may imply price support or guaranteed outcomes.
No agent may sign or submit the transaction.
Post-execution report must disclose amount, route, received assets, and reserve or liquidity destination.
items.publicDisclosure: Founder-held SATA movements are material events and must be disclosed. No price guarantee, no redemption promise, and liquidity can be thin and volatile.

items.title: Add 500000 sats to reach 1M sats
items.summary: Superseded direct BTC tranche proposal. The chairman rejected additional chairman-funded BTC for this step.
items.rationale: Reserve growth should proceed through operating revenue and approved asset-allocation proposals instead of requesting another direct BTC tranche.
items.proposedAction: No execution. Use the revenue-first reserve cycle proposal instead.
riskReview: No direct BTC tranche is requested.
No agent signs, broadcasts, or custodies any transaction.
Reserve growth must come from disclosed revenue, grants, donations, or pre-approved asset conversions.
Post-execution evidence is still required for any future reserve addition.
items.publicDisclosure: Proposed reserve tranche for the long-term 1,000,000,000 sats milestone. No price guarantee, no redemption promise, and no market-support commitment.

items.title: Run first 14-day revenue-first reserve cycle
items.summary: Use existing SATA proof tooling and public credibility to sell transparency services, then allocate approved proceeds toward BTC reserve growth, liquidity, and operating budget.
items.rationale: The project should generate operating revenue from the transparency/reporting infrastructure it already built instead of relying on new chairman-funded BTC tranches.
items.proposedAction: Approve revenue cycle 001 from revenue-operating-plan.json: sell $50 transparency audits first, then $150 report setup and $300 full proof-dashboard setup when qualified prospects ask for deeper work. Payment instructions, deliverables, conversions, reserve additions, and liquidity actions require chairman approval before execution.
riskReview: No agent may hold keys, receive funds, trade assets, or move BTC, SOL, SATA, USDC, or LP tokens.
No revenue pitch may promise SATA price movement, liquidity, investment return, redemption, or market support.
Client work must be factual transparency tooling or reporting, not fake engagement or paid investor targeting.
Any received funds need a separate allocation record before being converted, sent to reserve, or added to liquidity.
items.publicDisclosure: SATA may sell transparency tooling and public-reporting services. No price guarantee, no redemption promise, no revenue guarantee, and no market-support commitment.
